lines.text: Darius appoints 120 satraps and three administrators, and Daniel distinguishes himself, so the king plans to set him over the whole kingdom.
The officials find no corruption in Daniel, so they persuade Darius to sign a decree forbidding prayer to anyone but the king for sixty days.
Daniel keeps praying three times a day toward Jerusalem, and the king, though distressed, orders him thrown into the den of lions.
The king seals the stone and fasts, and at dawn Daniel says God sent a prophet to shut the lions' mouths.
The men who accused Daniel are thrown to the lions, and Darius decrees that all must fear Daniel's God, who rescued him.
